item.research_question: Does the AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy undergo tempering-like embrittlement, and if so, what are the underlying mechanisms driving the thermal evolution of its mechanical properties?
item.material_system: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) containing face-centered cubic (FCC) and ordered body-centered cubic (B2) phases
item.processing_route: Vacuum induction levitation melting followed by isothermal aging at 520, 600, 700, 750, 800, 1000, and 1200 °C for 20 hours at a heating rate of 300 °C/h and rapid quenching in water
item.test_conditions: Tensile testing at a constant strain rate of 1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹; impact toughness measurements; transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and atom probe tomography (APT) characterization of deformed and aged states
key_findings: Aging at 600 °C induces a ductile-to-brittle transition, where fracture elongation deteriorates significantly compared to the as-cast state.
Aging at 750 °C restores ductility, with fracture elongation rising dramatically to nearly three times that of the 600 °C aged alloy.
The 600 °C aged alloy exhibits L1₂ domains with an average diameter of ≈5.24 nm and a Ni/Al atomic ratio of ≈3:1, indicating a perfectly ordered Ni₃Al structure.
The 750 °C aged alloy shows larger L1₂ domains with an average diameter of ≈19.16 nm and an off-stoichiometric Ni/Al ratio of ≈2:1.
Jagged phase boundaries (PBs) with high interfacial energy form in the 600 °C aged alloy, whereas a Cr-rich particle (CRP)-free zone forms at the B2 edge in the 750 °C aged alloy.

The 600 °C aged alloy displays severe planar slip bands and dislocation pile-ups at phase boundaries, while the 750 °C aged alloy exhibits complex dislocation networks and multiple slip system activation.
DFT calculations reveal that the Ni₃Al-like L1₂ domains in the 600 °C alloy have a significantly higher antiphase boundary energy (APBE) and shear modulus than those in the 750 °C alloy.
item.mechanism: The ductile-to-brittle transition at 600 °C is driven by enhanced chemical ordering forming perfectly ordered L1₂ domains with high APBE, which promotes planar slip and strain localization, combined with the formation of jagged, low-coherency phase boundaries that act as stress concentrators. The subsequent brittle-to-ductile transition at 750 °C occurs because the L1₂ domains become off-stoichiometric and weakly ordered, facilitating cross-slip and uniform deformation, while the dissolution of Cr-rich particles creates a ductile, CRP-free zone at the phase boundaries that mitigates stress concentration.
item.limitations: The study focuses on a single AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 composition; the universality of this mechanism across other high-entropy alloys is not yet established.
item.future_work: Future efforts will extend these paradigms to other HEAs to evaluate the universality of the mechanism and guide safe high-temperature application, as well as probe the coupled thermal-mechanical-chemical effects on LCOs and PBs evolution.
quotes: Aging within the embrittlement‐prone regime enhances chemical ordering, increases the density of ordered domains, and induces jagged PBs, collectively triggering plastic instability and the ductile−to−brittle transition.
